cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: Market day. Half the town wants the towpath for stalls and the other half wants it for towing. The moot has asked the Keeper to say which half is right.

left.label: Stalls on the towpath
left.outcome: A slow day for boats, a good one for pies.

right.label: The towpath tows
right.outcome: The stalls go up Chapel Street. The pies are further away.

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: The Dray house has been Company property since the father left. I could take the lease and let it kindly to the daughter at a fair rent. Or the Keeper could go on living in it.

left.label: The Keeper stays
left.outcome: "Of course. It is a good house. I only mention it."

right.label: Let it to Mirren
right.outcome: Mirren pays Cole rent for her own house. She does not thank you.

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: The lock hands' children swim in the pound below the gate. Every summer I treat one for a paddle-wash. Every summer someone tells me it is how they learn. This summer I am telling you.

left.label: Fence the sill
left.outcome: The children swim from the Reed Reach instead, and the Hullfolk teach them.

right.label: It is how they learn
right.outcome: "So I hear. Every summer."

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A travelling puppet show wants to set up on the wharf. Its principal act, the handbill says, is 'The Lock Keeper Who Would Not Open'. The handbill has a drawing. It is not flattering.

left.label: Let them play
left.outcome: The town laughs for an hour, mostly at you. It helps, oddly.

right.label: Move them along
right.outcome: They play at the Reed Reach. The Hullfolk laugh instead.

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things. It's the hands' feast day. They want the chamber for the raft race. And last year the winner was Company mail, which nobody's forgotten.

left.label: The chamber for the race
left.outcome: Mirren wins on a door. The mail waits.

right.label: Race below the gate
right.outcome: "Right. Below. Where the current is." Nobody drowns. Nearly.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: Somebody from the Company measured my cellar this morning. For 'drainage'. Nobody measures a cellar for drainage. What does your Company want with my cellar?

left.label: Find out
left.outcome: Quenn, red-faced: the pound's leaking into the brewery well. It always has.

right.label: Drainage, presumably
right.outcome: "Presumably. Your Company presumes a lot."

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: The town wants a schoolroom. I have a building. The Company has a lease on it for 'future works' it has never begun. A word from the Keeper would release it.

left.label: Release the lease
left.outcome: Pell signs, sulking. Children arrive.

right.label: Future works are the Company's
right.outcome: "Of course. The children can wait. They are good at it."

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: A lock hand's wife is dying and wants to be taken down to her people on the Aldmere side. The flight is closed for repairs. I can keep her comfortable for two days. No more.

left.label: Open the flight for one boat
left.outcome: Quenn's crew stands aside. The boat goes down in silence.

right.label: She stays; make her comfortable
right.outcome: She dies at Halfway. Her people come up later.

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A young couple from the town ask the Keeper to witness their marriage at the top gate, at dawn, before the first boat. Hale is willing. The first boat is a Company mail packet.

left.label: Dawn, at the gate
left.outcome: The mail waits twenty minutes. The clerk cries, a little.

right.label: The chapel is for weddings
right.outcome: They marry in the chapel. It is fine. It is not the gate.

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things. A hand's been caught selling Company lamp oil at the inn. It's Perrin, who's got four children. And Vosk hasn't heard yet.

left.label: Dismiss him quietly
left.outcome: Perrin goes down the flight. The others learn it.

right.label: Dock his wages; keep him
right.outcome: "Right. I'll tell him. He'll cry. Then he'll work."

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The inn's out of Iron Spring and the well's low because the pound's low. I'm buying Sorrel beer at Sorrel prices. The town blames you, since the water's yours.

left.label: Subsidize the beer
left.outcome: The Coffers buy a town's goodwill by the barrel.

right.label: The water is nobody's
right.outcome: "Tell that to the well."

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: A tenant of mine, a lock hand, has not paid in two months. I could put him out. Or the Company could guarantee his rent from his wages, with your signature.

left.label: Guarantee the rent
left.outcome: Wages go to Cole before they go to the hand.

right.label: The Company does not guarantee rents
right.outcome: He is put out. He sleeps at the Reed Reach.

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: There is a case of the shakes at the inn: a bargee, feverish, insisting he drank nothing but the well water. I would like to test the well. Ilse would not like me to.

left.label: Test the well
left.outcome: Iron, and something else. Stroud's face does not change. Ilse's does.

right.label: It was the Sorrel beer
right.outcome: "Perhaps. I have seen worse. I have also seen wells."

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: An old bargeman, retiring, asks to name his last boat after the Keeper and paint it on the bow. He has already bought the paint. The Book has a fee for renaming.

left.label: Waive the fee
left.outcome: There is a coal barge with your name on it. It goes east forever.

right.label: The fee is the fee
right.outcome: He pays it, and names the boat something else.

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things, and these are good ones. The hands have finished the new bollards early. They want the afternoon. And Perrin's wife has had a fifth.

left.label: Give them the afternoon
left.outcome: The wharf is empty and cheerful. Boats wait and do not mind.

right.label: Finish the week's work first
right.outcome: "Right." Perrin's fifth waits with everyone else.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The moot's asked me to stand for reeve again and I've said I'll do it if the Keeper comes to the moot. Once. To listen. Nobody's asked a Keeper before. They're not sure you're allowed.

left.label: Come to the moot
left.outcome: You listen for three hours. It changes how the town looks at you.

right.label: The Keeper answers to the Company
right.outcome: "Right. I stand anyway. Remember I asked."

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: I have been asked to fund the Jubilee bunting and have said I will if the Keeper agrees to a small plaque on the Company house. My name. Modest lettering.

left.label: A modest plaque
left.outcome: The lettering is not modest.

right.label: The Company funds its own bunting
right.outcome: "Of course. Quite right. Kindly remember I offered."

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: You have not slept a full night in a week. I can see it from here. Dray did this. I am not saying you are Dray. I am saying I have seen the end of it.

left.label: Sleep tonight; Dace has the gate
left.outcome: You sleep. You dream about the gauge.

right.label: After the season
right.outcome: "That is what he said."

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A boy from the town has been caught riding the paddle beam as the gate opens. It is the best thing he has ever done, he says. His mother wants him whipped. The hands want him hired.

left.label: Hire him
left.outcome: Dace gets an apprentice who is afraid of nothing.

right.label: His mother's decision
right.outcome: He is whipped, and rides the beam again the next week.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: It's the day my son drowned. Every year the town leaves a lamp on the sill and every year the Company takes it off for the first boat. This year I'm asking the Keeper first.

left.label: The lamp stays all day
left.outcome: The first boat waits for the lamp. The bargee knew the story.

right.label: Until the first boat, as ever
right.outcome: "As ever." She takes the lamp off herself.
